findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer tests the installation-not-found path.
findings.body: The test used to assert "The GitHub installation could not be found." Now it sends a `state` (`ddd023...`) that does not match the pipeline signature and asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." That error comes from the state-mismatch check in OAuthLoginView, so the request never reaches `build_integration` or the stubbed 404, and the 404 handling has no test. Fix: send the correct state, stub the OAuth token and `/user` endpoints, and keep asserting the not-found message. Test the state mismatch in a separate test.

findings.title: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError when the metadata has no sender.
findings.body: This lookup assumes every active Integration has `metadata["sender"]`. That key is set by the installation webhook. Integrations created through `build_integration`, or before that webhook handling existed, may not have it. One such case is an Integration that is still active after every OrganizationIntegration was removed: re-installing it would raise a KeyError and return a 500 instead of a clean error page. I could not see the code that fills in the metadata to confirm it is missing. Fix: use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and show `error(...)` when it is missing.

findings.title: Token exchange network errors are not caught and become a 500.
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` runs outside the `try`. If the call to GitHub's access_token endpoint fails (timeout, connection error, blocked by safe_urlopen), the exception escapes and the user gets a 500 instead of the installation-failed dialog. The dialog's postMessage also never reaches the opener window. Fix: move the `safe_urlopen` call inside the `try` and return `error(...)` on failure.
